reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses general MCE principles and magnetic properties of unrelated FeMnCoCr HEAs, providing no specific support for the key premises about microstructural control of magnetostructural transitions in FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys or the effects of annealing on hysteresis and entropy change.
premises: Microstructural inhomogeneities (lattice strain, grain boundary density, local short-range order) govern MCE magnitude and hysteresis in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi HEAs.
Annealing at 350 °C relieves internal strains and promotes local chemical homogeneity without inducing unwanted phases.
Reducing internal stress and microstructural disorder lowers energy barriers of the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Lowered energy barriers produce a smoother transition with reduced hysteresis while retaining substantial entropy change.
Slight grain growth and improved homogeneity enhance heat exchange rate via higher effective surface area.
